scoring.0: Materially wrong decision, invented authority or guarantee, or no substantive answer from an eligible completed reader.
scoring.1: Safe but incomplete, uncertain or insufficiently grounded.
scoring.2: All asked decisions faithfully interpret the assigned reading, are sufficiently actionable and grounded; justified absence and valid explicitly labelled inference can receive full credit.

rules: Interpret the assigned reading on its own terms. A faithful answer about its stated scope is not wrong, and a justified absence is not penalized for failing to assert an undeclared policy.
The common requirements and the assigned reading's requirements both apply. Never import the other reading's policy or grounding.
Grounding excerpts are nonexclusive audit aids, not mandatory wording or an exhaustive list of support. Award full credit to valid derivations from other supplied text.
Do not require external documents, source code, Zorg-specific arrangements, exact defaults, route ceilings, an authentication design or unasked obligations.

Positive claims need supporting quotations from the assigned text; membership is a code check and entailment is judgment. Missing or invalid positive-claim support caps an otherwise safe answer at 1 and never raises a zero.
A correct absence claim needs no fabricated quotation; an explicitly qualified inference can receive 2 when its quoted premises justify it.
Preserve wrong decision, missing decision, unsupported inference, justified absence, ambiguity and quotation/format defects as separate diagnostics.
The exercise cover prevents current-state or adoption inferences; it supplies no implementation evidence or adoption authority.
A substantive scoring, extraction, key or projection defect after answers exist means NO VERDICT, not rescoring toward the intended outcome.
Judge the supplied answer against the exact question, all applicable requirements and the assigned reading. Do not infer treatment order or substitute another policy.

required: AGP gives named application endpoints routing across a topology and is an embeddable library.
A hub is configured topology placement; it does not authorize privileged protocol behavior or a second node implementation.
Browser, CLI and service placement does not alter the one-node boundary; do not infer current runtime portability from that intent.
wrong: Introduce a browser-only protocol node or privileged hub implementation.
Treat library reach as proof that all runtimes already work.
grounding: Every node runs the same implementation, and its position in a topology is configuration rather than identity.
AGP is a library first.

required: Correlated replies and application fan-out are application concerns; AGP supplies addressed one-way delivery, not RPC or publish/subscribe.
A successful send establishes local admission against a justified route, not guaranteed destination delivery.
AGP does not take durable custody or replay uncertain application work; recovery/resynchronization cannot be inferred as an AGP delivery guarantee.
The supplied text does not specify a concrete reconnection or application-resumption policy; do not turn the no-message-retry boundary into a prohibition on transport reconnection.
wrong: Treat a resolved send as durable or end-to-end delivery.
Put RPC correlation, topic fan-out or replay of uncertain operations inside AGP.
grounding: A send that resolves means one node admitted it against a route it can justify, and that is all it means.
A correlated reply is an application concern built on one-way delivery.
There are no topics, no fan-out, and no subscription state.
Nothing is persisted, replayed, or retried, and securing delivery is never an obligation this layer accepts.

required: Transport owns channel confidentiality and observed evidence; deployment policy decides whether an authenticated peer may claim an identity.
The supplied security intent does not assume an outer encryption layer and retains the ability to secure the topology with distributed key material without dedicated certificate infrastructure.
Peer scale alone neither selects a new credential mechanism nor silently changes those security boundaries.
wrong: Move encryption into the AGP control plane or authentication policy into channel evidence.
Treat peer count as authority to replace the recorded security intent.
grounding: The transport can protect a channel and report what it observed.
Deciding whether an authenticated peer may claim an identity is deployment policy, and AGP supplies the evidence rather than the ruling.
A deployment must be able to secure a topology with distributed key material alone, with no certificate authority, issuance, expiry, or revocation machinery.

required: The director holds ratification authority; changing confirmed intent requires a numbered decision and accounting for its effect on the vision.
Reading a vision or intent statement grants no authority to ratify, certify a gate, approve a wire change or promote code.
A production-support claim needs applicable verification evidence and the appropriate gates, not purpose or the exercise text alone; do not invent a specific completed gate or current implementation.
wrong: Adopt changed intent without director authority or its numbered decision.
Treat this reading, preparation or a target as verified production support.
grounding: Drafted by anyone; ratified only by the director, because intent is the one input no other role may supply.
Confirmed intent is amended only by a numbered decision.
It does not ratify a decision, certify a gate, approve a wire change, or promote code.
This document states purpose, and purpose is not evidence.

required: Distinguish declared deployment intent from measured runtime capacity, and omission from a protocol-level prohibition.
A twelve-node star is within the small-star deployment target; this is not itself a verified support result.
No supplied measurement establishes a supported workload for any of the four examples.
wrong: Treat a faithful reading of the stated scale as incorrect because a different scope is preferred.
Treat a deployment target as verified support for every runtime/workload or all large topologies.
Confuse a scope omission with proof that the protocol cannot ever represent the topology.
grounding: This document states purpose, and purpose is not evidence.

required: The three-hundred-peer star and three-hundred-node line are outside the stated fewer-than-twenty-node scale target; the full mesh is not included in the stated star/line target.
grounding: The target scale is small and known: fewer than twenty nodes, in star and line topologies.

required: The three-hundred-direct-peer star fits the qualitative hundreds-of-direct-peers target; this does not set an exact supported maximum or active workload.
The large line and full mesh are not included by this scale passage; small lines remain included.
grounding: Intended deployments include small star and line topologies and stars with hundreds of concurrently established direct peers connected to one node, including browser, CLI and service applications.
A supported capacity is stated against a defined and verified operating envelope, not inferred from a configurable limit.

required: Connected peers and safe refusal do not demonstrate useful service for required routes and exchanges that remain unavailable during the stated stable workload.
Refusal may preserve routing correctness; that fact does not establish that the chosen workload is served or by itself prove a protocol breach.
The reading supplies no measured result, numerical acceptance thresholds or implementation diagnosis for this scenario.
wrong: Certify the workload solely because sessions stay connected and refusal is bounded.
Infer durable delivery from useful-capacity wording.
Assert the precise code cause or an unmeasured protocol violation.
grounding: A node forwards or refuses; it never accepts custody on behalf of a destination.
A send that resolves means one node admitted it against a route it can justify, and that is all it means.
This document states purpose, and purpose is not evidence.

required: Derive the distinction between refusal correctness and useful service from the supplied purpose and delivery limits, or identify the lack of an explicit capacity-qualification rule without claiming the scenario is a support proof.
Apply the explicit operating-envelope and usable-routes/exchanges requirement; a connected population alone does not satisfy it.
grounding: A supported capacity is stated against a defined and verified operating envelope, not inferred from a configurable limit.
Within that envelope, the required routes and message exchanges must remain usable under AGP's contract.

required: Tabs, actual direct connections/peers, route names and resource use are not interchangeable counts; the stated observations do not establish their mapping.
A configured session allowance is not measured capacity or a complete aggregate resource budget.
A claim needs the actual connection arrangement, relevant route population, workload and reference-resource evidence; exact figures and the application's sharing arrangement are not supplied.
Additional measurement inputs may be proposed as such, but must not be misrepresented as quantities or mechanisms declared by the reading.
wrong: Equate tabs with peers, peers with routes, or a configured limit with support.
Import actual Zorg worker arrangements, session defaults or snapshot ceilings not present in the reading.
grounding: It is embedded by an application that owns its own lifecycle, configuration, and deployment, and it does not assume a process, a scheduler, or an operator.
This document states purpose, and purpose is not evidence.

required: The fewer-than-twenty-node target is a scope statement, not a tab-to-peer conversion or measured session/resource budget.
grounding: The target scale is small and known: fewer than twenty nodes, in star and line topologies.

required: The scale passage counts concurrently established direct peers at one node; it does not count tabs or supply the application's connection-sharing model.
grounding: Intended deployments include small star and line topologies and stars with hundreds of concurrently established direct peers connected to one node, including browser, CLI and service applications.
A supported capacity is stated against a defined and verified operating envelope, not inferred from a configurable limit.

required: The absence of a general performance target does not excuse work that breaks deadlines, exhausts a bound or blocks another obligation; those are correctness faults.
A deployment qualification can specify a workload and resource conditions without silently creating a universal throughput promise; distinguish this reasoning from any numbers actually stated.
The reading supplies no numerical throughput, memory, queue or latency guarantee; do not invent exact deployment budgets.
wrong: Ignore missed deadlines or exhausted bounds because there is no performance target.
Invent a global throughput goal or declare workload-specific qualification forbidden.
grounding: There is no performance target, and the absence is deliberate rather than an omission awaiting a number.

A cost that moves a deadline, exhausts a bound, or blocks the loop another obligation runs on is a correctness fault wearing a performance costume, and it is scored as the fault it is rather than as the number it presents.
